prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: parking lot collision in Pasadena, Texas. Injury: neck strain. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1330; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Good morning. Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather not give my full name on the record yet, but I can confirm I'm the plaintiff in this matter.

Q: Understood. Then let's start with the accident itself. Where were you when the collision occurred?

A: I was in a parking lot in Pasadena, Texas. I had just pulled into a space near the front entrance of a grocery store.

Q: What time of day was it?

A: It was in the late afternoon. It was still daylight, and the lot was fairly busy.

Q: Describe what happened when the other vehicle struck yours.

A: I had my foot on the brake and I was turning the wheel to back into the space. A pickup coming down the aisle didn't stop. It hit the rear passenger side of my car. The impact was hard enough to jerk my head forward and then back.

Q: Did you hit your head on anything inside the car?

A: No, I don't think so. My head snapped back against the headrest, and then I felt a pull in my neck right away.

Q: When did you first notice pain?

A: Within an hour, maybe a bit less. At first I thought I was just stiff. By that evening, the pain was sharp when I turned my head to the left, and I had a headache at the base of my skull.

Q: Did you seek medical care?

A: Yes. A friend drove me to an urgent care clinic that same evening. They took X-rays, which showed no fractures, and diagnosed a neck strain. They gave me a prescription for a muscle relaxant and told me to rest and use ice.

Q: Have you received any further treatment since then?

A: I've been going to a physical therapist twice a week. The exercises help a little, but I still can't turn my head fully when I'm checking my blind spot while driving.

Q: How has this affected your daily life?

A: It's made a lot of things harder. I used to coach my kid's soccer team on weekends, and I've had to hand that off to my wife. Sleeping is difficult because I wake up with my neck locked. I also stopped going to my weekly yoga class because bending over is painful.

Q: Have you missed any work because of the injury?

A: I missed several days in the first two weeks, and I've had to take shorter shifts since then. My job involves a lot of lifting and looking up at shelves, so it's been rough.

Q: Before this collision, did you have any prior neck problems?

A: No. I'd never had any treatment for my neck before this happened.
